      "contextEndEvent": 457,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "we don't need the fourth criterion for the obvious reason that God is postulated as the explanation of everything.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Swinburne removes background-knowledge fit from assessment because the proposed explanation encompasses everything, renewing E244–251 within the same argument. This could exclude relevant counterevidence, but he supplies a methodological reason and still requires explanatory fit. It remains unclear whether evidence is excluded altogether or incorporated as data needing explanation."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1138,
      "endEvent": 1149,
      "contextStartEvent": 1052,
      "contextEndEvent": 1199,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "if the phenomena we're trying to explain covers more or less everything, then there isn't anything outside that scope.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Responding to Millican's objection, Swinburne again rejects an independent background-knowledge constraint through an explicit scope argument. Whether this neutralizes contrary evidence remains unclear: E1060–1081 requires abandoning predictions contradicted by data, while E1150–1199 limits the explanatory claim and appeals to physics. The disputed methodological argument is not slogan substitution."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1436,
      "endEvent": 1440,
      "contextStartEvent": 1421,
      "contextEndEvent": 1473,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "we should be grateful for that, whatever else happens.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The unconditional gratitude formula could discourage criticism of suffering, but its stated object is being created, not every divine action. E1421–1438 supplies a parent–creator analogy and a claimed entitlement to permit suffering. Those contestable reasons prevent slogan substitution; the text does not clearly make gratitude cancel all moral objections."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1480,
      "endEvent": 1491,
      "contextStartEvent": 1463,
      "contextEndEvent": 1525,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "it will be a compensation in the sense that their total life will be a good life.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Any earthly life judged not worth living triggers a guaranteed compensating afterlife, repeated through E1523. This makes even the conceded worst cases compatible with divine goodness without independent evidence of compensation. Swinburne supplies a conditional moral argument and surgical analogy, so this is a protected non-slogan argument, not unsupported slogan substitution."
    }
  ],
